messages.subject: uls -ulsmv fit indices
parts:
Dear community,

I am conducting a CFA with categorical variables and I have three questions:

  1. Would you recommend using the ULS or the ULSMV estimator?

  2. Regarding model fit indices, is it advisable to examine the same indices as when using WLSMV (CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR)?
    2.1. Would the acceptable cutoff values for these indices be the same?

  3. Would these recommendations change depending on the sample size? I am working with two samples, one with approximately 220 cases and another with 1,810 cases.

Thank you very much in advance.
Best regards,


En virtud de la Ley Nº20.393, sobre Responsabilidad Penal de las Personas Jurídicas por los delitos señalados en su artículo 1°, Fundación Luksic (“FL”) tiene implementado un Modelo de Prevención de Delitos. Debido a lo anterior, toda comunicación a través de correos electrónicos, entre los trabajadores de FL y funcionarios públicos, proveedores y terceros en general, debe realizarse utilizando las direcciones de correo electrónico institucionales, es decir, no pueden efectuarse a través de correos electrónicos privados.

According to Law No. 20,393, regarding the Criminal Liability of Legal Entities for the offenses indicated in its article 1, Fundación Luksic (“FL”) has implemented a Crime Prevention Model. As a result, all communication through emails between FL employees and public officials, suppliers and third parties in general, must take place using institutional email addresses; that is, they cannot be conducted through private email accounts.

messages.subject: Re: uls -ulsmv fit indices
parts: 1. Would you recommend using the ULS or the ULSMV estimator?

I think for ordinal data "ulsmv" is a better option than "uls". and if your sample size is not low, "wlsmv" is better than "ulsmv" but you can compare results for both methods and if they are the same you can use wlsmv.
